rule_level_problems.problem: Dark patches vs light patches distinction relies on Hyperpigmentation/Hypopigmentation; Hyperpigmentation sites are body-structure qualified, so patches on other sites match nothing and the venous stasis/melasma rules cannot be told apart from plain hyperpigmentation features (red-brown, spidery veins) that the page uses.
ANDs generalised congenital achromia, white hair and iris hypopigmentation; a patient lacking one of the three recorded findings gets no albinism suggestion. Defensible but strict.
Fires on any patchy achromia, with no exclusion for the other conditions. Page-faithful.
Temperature and systolic BP are used in the priority rule but absent from check_for (measurements, acceptable). Check list and priority rule otherwise agree.

summary: The rules encode the page well: all red-box criteria except Hb (not_representable) are in both the check list and the Urgent priority rule, and each 'likely' diagnosis has a probable rule with sensible SNOMED concepts. The most consequential gaps are the dropped Hb threshold and the lost hepatitis A IgM flowchart branch with its acute hepatitis A conclusion. The 'any medication' criterion is very broad and the descriptive discriminators (red-brown, spidery veins, flat brown) are not encoded.
